newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba could free repos from reserves today - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Buba could free repos from reserves today - dealers.

text.p: German money market dealers hold out hopes the Bundesbank may announce plans to free securities repurchase, or repo, business from minimum reserves after its regularly scheduled meeting on Thursday.
"The hope is there that the Bundesbank will make such an announcement today," said a trader at a major German bank, asking not to be named.
Traders said such a step could help Germany regain business lost to London, thereby giving the German financial centre a boost.
"Such a step would help us tremendously," another dealer added, also asking not to be named.

Bundesbank vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum several weeks ago said the Bundesbank planned to set the repos free, in a bid to give the German financial centre a boost in the runup to Europe's planned currency union. But he did not give a specific date for when the step may be taken.

Senior bankers have long complained the Bundesbank's restrictive minimum reserve requirements, forcing them to hold two percent of sight deposits and 1.5 percent of savings deposits in non-interest bearing accounts at the central bank, helped erode their competitive advantage.
The Bundesbank is not expected to change its key interest rates at today's meeting, dealers said.
